name: How do paint touch ups on baseboards and trim differ from walls?

mainEntity.name: How do paint touch ups on baseboards and trim differ from walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Baseboards, doors, and trim usually feature semi-gloss or satin enamel, which reflects light more than wall paint and reveals brush marks easily. Touching up trim requires thorough cleaning to remove foot scuffs, light scuff-sanding to help adhesion, and feathering along the natural grain or profile lines. When trim has multiple chips across a single board, painting the full run of molding provides a cleaner result than spot patching.
acceptedAnswer.description: Trim uses higher-sheen enamel that shows brush marks easily, requiring light sanding and feathering along the molding profile to blend properly.
